public_rationale: The claim forecasts that the generative AI race will never be winner-take-all. It has no deadline. Under the contract, it can be settled early only as contradicted. That requires dated evidence that one country or firm has taken essentially the whole market and shut out its rivals. A forecast of this kind cannot be confirmed early. The packet has one evidence item, a TechCrunch article dated 2025-07-31 on a Menlo Ventures report (e1). Per that report, Anthropic held 32% and OpenAI 25% of enterprise large language model market share by usage. The report predates the December 2025 post and covers one point in time. It is context only and cannot show what happens later. No item in the packet meets the early-contradiction rule, so the forecast stays open.
limitations: The only market figures in the packet come from one Menlo Ventures report on enterprise LLM market share by usage, published in July 2025 and cited by TechCrunch. The report predates the post.
The packet does not say which countries the enterprise figures cover. It has no data on Chinese providers or on use across borders.
The packet has no market data from after the December 2025 post.

our_interpretation: Read in context as mainly about the US-China race, and secondarily about firms.
'Winner take all' means one country (or firm) ends up with essentially the whole generative AI market, pushing rivals out.
No deadline is given ('ever'), so the forecast stays open unless the outcome is decisively settled.
criteria.support_condition: Over a long period, both countries and several firms keep large, lasting shares of generative AI use and supply, with no single winner pushing the other out.
criteria.contradiction_condition: One country or firm ends up with essentially the whole global generative AI market, excluding its rivals.

evidence.explanation: In mid-2025, enterprise use was split among several firms with no single winner. This is a snapshot and cannot settle a forecast about 'ever'.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Long-run market share or deployment data for US and Chinese generative AI providers, from independent surveys, company filings, or official statistics. Data showing several countries and firms keeping large shares would fit the forecast, but cannot confirm a 'never' forecast.
